paragraphs: We are a medical technology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative, minimally invasive solutions for patients with obstructive sleep apnea ("OSA"). Our proprietary Inspire system is the first FDA, European Union ("EU") Regulation No. 2017/745 ("MDR" or "EU Medical Devices Regulation"), and Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency-approved neurostimulation technology of its kind that provides a safe and effective treatment for patients with moderate to severe OSA. We have developed a novel, closed-loop solution that continuously monitors a patient's breathing and delivers mild hypoglossal nerve stimulation to maintain an open airway. A significant body of clinical data, which includes a publication in the New England Journal of Medicine, multiple publications in leading respiratory, ear, nose and throat ("ENT") and sleep medicine journals, and more than 385 peer-reviewed publications, supports the safety and efficacy of Inspire therapy. Inspire therapy received premarket approval ("PMA") from the FDA in 2014 and has been commercially available in certain European markets since 2011. Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare ("MLHW") approved Inspire therapy to treat moderate to severe OSA in 2018. Inspire therapy is indicated for patients with moderate to severe OSA who do not have significant central sleep apnea and do not have a complete concentric collapse of the airway at the soft palate level. Physicians have treated more than 125,000 patients with Inspire therapy across the United States ("U.S."), Europe, and Asia.

Sleep apnea is a serious and chronic disease that negatively impacts a patient's sleep, health, and quality of life. OSA is the most common form of sleep apnea. OSA occurs when a person's breathing is interrupted during sleep by a partially or completely blocked airway and affects patients of all ages, sexes, and body types. The severity of OSA is measured by the number of partial or complete airway blockages that a patient experiences in an hour, referred to as the apnea-hypopnea index ("AHI"). Moderate OSA patients have an AHI of 15 to 30 events per hour, while severe OSA patients have an AHI of 30 more events per hour. Left untreated, OSA increases the risk of high blood pressure, hypertension, heart failure, stroke, coronary artery disease, and other life-threatening diseases.

Continuous positive airway pressure ("CPAP") is the leading therapy for patients with moderate to severe OSA. CPAP is delivered through a face or nasal mask that connects through a hose to a bedside air pump. In order for CPAP to be most effective, the mask must form an airtight seal on the patient's face or nose and the mask must be worn every night. The effectiveness of CPAP has been limited by low patient compliance as many patients find the mask or treatment cumbersome, uncomfortable, and loud. When CPAP fails or cannot be tolerated, patients' remaining treatment options consist primarily of invasive surgical procedures developed to modify or remove existing tissue in an attempt to create free air flow. These invasive surgical procedures have limited or unpredictable clinical benefit, are irreversible, and can be extremely painful.

We believe that there continues to be both an urgent clinical need and a strong market opportunity for an alternative to CPAP that is effective and minimally invasive. Data shows that patients with CPAP intolerant OSA have a higher risk for mortality than patients with CPAP-tolerant OSA and higher healthcare utilization rates based on increased cardiovascular health risks. Two findings published in 2022 from Medicare and the French national healthcare insurance databases have demonstrated, in large national cohorts, risks of CPAP intolerance. Specifically, Medicare patients with CPAP intolerance had higher risks of new cardiovascular events than those who were adherent. Similarly, the French national reimbursement database showed that in over 176,000 patients, CPAP non-adherent patients had a higher risk for mortality and new onset of heart failure than those who were adherent. These findings show the urgency of treating CPAP-intolerant OSA to improve patient outcomes and potentially reduce healthcare utilization.

Inspire therapy is an innovative, closed-loop, minimally invasive solution designed to provide comfort and convenience, and which results in high compliance for patients with moderate to severe OSA. Once implanted, the Inspire system delivers electrical stimulation that causes a slight forward movement of the back of the tongue, which helps to maintain an open airway, enabling the patient to inhale freely without interruption. We believe our Inspire therapy provides the following benefits:
•Safe, effective, and durable treatment supported by compelling clinical data, including long-term efficacy results out to five years from initial treatment.
•Closed-loop system that uses a proprietary algorithm to continuously monitor patients' breathing and provide electrical stimulation during the inspiratory phase.

•Comfortable and convenient therapy resulting in high patient satisfaction that was reported to be 90% in patients who were followed an average of 12 months from initial treatment, according to the most recent publication of our ongoing global patient registry.
•Strong patient compliance, with 80% of patients reporting continued nightly use through five years from initial treatment in our Stimulation Therapy for Apnea Reduction ("STAR") trial.
•Minimally invasive outpatient procedure with short recovery time.
•Long-lasting solution with a battery designed to last approximately 11 years without charging or maintenance.

The results from multiple clinical studies, which include seven sponsored and more than 100 independent clinical studies that evaluated several thousand patients, have shown that our Inspire therapy provides statistically significant and sustained reduction in the severity of patients' OSA, improvement in sleep-related quality of life and reduction in snoring, as well as high patient compliance rates and a strong safety profile.

Our pivotal STAR trial was designed to demonstrate longitudinal therapy efficacy and included a randomized controlled therapy withdrawal study. The longitudinal study demonstrated an approximately 70% reduction in the median AHI in patients with moderate to severe OSA from a baseline of 29.3 events per hour to 9.0 events per hour at 12 months following initial treatment. STAR trial follow-up has shown results similar to the initial data at 18 months, three years, and five years following initial treatment. At five years, median AHI in patients with moderate to severe OSA remained low at 6.2 events per hour. The effectiveness of Inspire therapy was further demonstrated by the results of the randomized controlled therapy withdrawal study, in which patients in the therapy withdrawal group regressed to near-baseline AHI levels while patients in the control group that continued therapy experienced sustained therapeutic benefits.

In addition to the STAR trial, we have established a global real-world patient registry ("ADHERE") to collect data on safety, effectiveness, weekly usage, overall compliance, and satisfaction from patients who have been implanted with an Inspire system for one year after implant. The target enrollment of 5,000 patients was achieved in 2024 and patient follow-up was completed in 2025 with final results pending analysis. For more details on ADHERE, please see the section titled "Clinical Results and Studies—ADHERE Patient Registry" below.

headings: Our revenue is primarily generated from sales of our Inspire system and we are, therefore, highly dependent on it for our success.
Our financial results and the market price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly and may not fully reflect the underlying performance of our business.
We may not be able to sustain profitability, we have historically incurred significant operating losses, and we may incur operating losses in the future.
Our long-term growth depends on our ability to enhance our Inspire system, expand our indications, and develop and commercialize additional products.
Our results of operations could be materially harmed if we are unable to accurately forecast customer demand for our Inspire system and manage our inventory.

Performance issues, service interruptions or price increases by our shipping carriers could adversely affect our business and harm our reputation and ability to provide our services on a timely basis.
If we are unable to effectively size, manage and maintain our direct sales and marketing organization we may not be able to generate revenue growth.
To successfully market and sell our Inspire system in markets outside of the U.S., we must address many international business risks.

We face the risk of product liability claims that could be expensive, divert management's attention and harm our reputation and business. We may not be able to maintain adequate product liability insurance.
If the quality of our Inspire system does not meet the expectations of physicians or patients, then our brand and reputation or our business could be adversely affected.

If we choose to acquire new and complementary businesses, products or technologies, we may be unable to complete these acquisitions or to successfully integrate them in a cost-effective and non-disruptive manner.
Unfavorable global economic conditions could adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Failure of a key information technology system, process or site, cyberattacks, or other deficiencies in our cybersecurity could have an adverse effect on our business and operations.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. These risks include, but are not limited to, those described below, each of which may be relevant to an investment decision. You should carefully consider the risks described below, together with the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The realization of any of the following risks could have a significant adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations, growth, and our ability to accomplish our strategic objectives. In that event, the trading price of our common stock could decline. Other events that we do not currently anticipate or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our reputation, business, financial conditions, results of operations, growth, and our ability to accomplish our strategic objectives.

We began selling our Inspire system in 2011 in certain European countries, in 2014 in the U.S., and in 2021 in certain Asia Pacific regions. Sales of our Inspire system accounted for primarily all of our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023. We expect that sales of our Inspire system will continue to account for the substantial majority of our revenue going forward. Our ability to execute our growth strategy and remain profitable will therefore depend upon the adoption by patients, physicians, and sleep centers, among others, of our Inspire therapy to treat moderate to severe OSA in patients who are unable to use or get consistent benefit from CPAP.

We cannot ensure that our Inspire therapy will achieve or maintain broad market acceptance among physicians and patients. As a single-product company, any failure of the Inspire system to satisfy physician or patient demand or to achieve meaningful market acceptance will harm our business and future prospects.

The market price of our common stock and our quarterly and annual results of operations have in the past and may in the future vary significantly and future period-to-period comparisons of our operating results may not be meaningful. Accordingly, the results of any one quarter or period should not be relied upon as an indication of future performance. The market price of our common stock and our quarterly and annual financial results may fluctuate as a result of a variety of factors, many of which are outside our control and, as a result, may not fully reflect the underlying performance of our business. Such factors may include, for example, seasonal variations in our sales or required postponements of elective surgical procedures effected during a health crisis, as was the

case with COVID-19. We generally experience and may in the future experience higher sales in the U.S. during the fourth quarter as a result of patients having paid their annual insurance deductibles in full, thereby reducing their out-of-pocket costs. Alternatively, in the first quarter, many U.S. patients' insurance deductibles reset, requiring more out-of-pocket costs, which negatively impacts our sales during this period.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our financial statements and the related notes to those statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical financial information, the following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions. Some of the numbers included herein have been rounded for the convenience of presentation. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those discussed under Part I. "Item 1A. Risk Factors'' and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are a medical technology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative, minimally invasive solutions for patients with obstructive sleep apnea ("OSA"). Our proprietary Inspire system is the only FDA, European Union ("EU") Medical Devices Regulation ("MDR"), and Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency-approved neurostimulation technology of its kind that provides a safe and effective treatment for patients with moderate to severe OSA. We have developed a novel, closed-loop solution that continuously monitors a patient's breathing and delivers mild hypoglossal nerve stimulation to maintain an open airway. Inspire therapy is indicated for patients with moderate to severe OSA who do not have significant central sleep apnea and do not have a complete concentric collapse of the airway at the soft palate level.

We sell our Inspire system to hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers ("ASCs") in the U.S. and in select countries in Europe and Japan through a direct sales organization and we sell our Inspire system in Singapore, Hong Kong, and Thailand through distributors. Our direct sales force engages in sales efforts and promotional activities primarily focused on ENT physicians and sleep centers. In addition, we highlight our compelling clinical data and value proposition to increase awareness and adoption amongst referring physicians. We build upon this top-down approach with strong direct-to-consumer marketing initiatives to create awareness of the benefits of our Inspire system and drive interest through patient empowerment. We believe this outreach helps to educate thousands of patients on our Inspire therapy.

Although our sales and marketing efforts are directed at patients and physicians because they are the primary users of our technology, we consider the hospitals and ASCs where the procedure is performed to be our customers, as they are the purchasing agents of our Inspire system. Our customers are reimbursed according to the coding and correlated payment by various third-party payors, such as commercial payors and government healthcare programs. Our Inspire system is currently covered on a per-patient basis for patients insured by commercial payors, under Local Coverage Determinations for patients insured by Medicare and Medicare Advantage, and under U.S. government contract for patients who are treated by the Veterans Health Administration. As of February 13, 2026, we have secured positive coverage policies with many U.S. commercial payors, including all large national commercial insurers, covering more than 300 million lives in the U.S. In addition, all seven Medicare Administrative Contractors provide coverage of Inspire therapy when certain coverage criteria are met.

Third-party payors require physicians and hospitals to identify the service for which they are seeking reimbursement by using Current Procedural Terminology ("CPT") codes, which are created and maintained by the American Medical Association. Our various generations of Inspire therapy have been billed under different codes and reimbursement approaches throughout our history. For example, the procedures performed to implant our Inspire IV device are described for billing purposes using Category I CPT code 64582. And for 2025, the procedures performed to implant our Inspire V device were described for billing purposes using Category I CPT code 64568. There are also other relevant CPT codes for revisions, explants and DISE.

In November 2025, the final 2026 Medicare reimbursement payments were announced. There has been, and still is currently, confusion on the appropriate reimbursement and coding for our products from CMS and Medicare Administrative Contractors ("MACs"), as well as other payors and stakeholders in the overall reimbursement and coding process. Most recently, we received clarification regarding the coding that should be used for the Inspire V procedure. Currently, healthcare centers and physicians should bill the most recent healthcare policies, be it a Medicare Administrative Contractor (MACs) or a commercial payor, and based on this clarification, we believe the

code will transition to CPT code 64582 for the Inspire V procedure, including the use of a -52 modifier. To date, our top commercial payers by volume have all adopted the guidance of 64568 for coding and reimbursement of Inspire V. Confusion will remain until there is definitive and public guidance from various stakeholders and we have sufficient claims data that has been submitted and processed across payers. The resulting coding and reimbursement decisions may impact our business, financial condition and results of operations, in particular our future revenues. We continue to work with the relevant stakeholders to get specific and accurate direction for Inspire V coding, including the -52 modifier that we would expect to reduce the professional fee for Inspire V procedures under CPT code 64582 by approximately 10% to 50% of the base rate. In any case, we believe that a significant decrease in the professional fee resulting from use of the –52 modifier will likely influence physicians' willingness to perform the Inspire V procedure and may limit the number of cases they choose to undertake. Beyond our short-term initiatives intended to minimize the actual reduction applied to the professional fee, as well as to drive consistency across the country, we are seeking a long-term solution, including the creation of a separate CPT code. There can be no guarantee as to the timing or outcome of the CPT code to be applied.
Reimbursement in other countries can often be established through a combination of private (commercial insurance) and public funding sources, or at the hospital level through innovation budgets.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, 95.6% of our revenue was derived in the U.S. and 4.4% was derived outside of the U.S. No single customer accounted for more than 10% of our revenue.

We rely on third-party suppliers to manufacture our Inspire system and its components. Many of these suppliers are currently single source suppliers. Currently, all of our manufacturing is done in the U.S. and most components for our Inspire system are sourced in the U.S. We have experienced supply disruptions in the past.

We typically seek to maintain higher levels of inventory to protect ourselves from supply interruptions, and, as a result, we are subject to the risk of inventory obsolescence and expiration, which could lead to inventory impairment charges. For example, during 2025, we recorded a charge of $2.1 million for excess component parts related to our Inspire IV system.

Since our inception in 2007, we have financed our operations primarily through sales of our Inspire system, private placements of our convertible preferred securities, amounts borrowed under our former credit facility, and equity offerings of our common stock. We have devoted significant resources to research and development activities related to our Inspire system, including clinical and regulatory initiatives to obtain marketing approval, and sales and marketing activities. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated revenue of $912.0 million with a gross margin of 85.4% and net income of $145.4 million, compared to revenue of $802.8 million with a gross margin of 84.7% and net income of $53.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, and revenue of $624.8 million with a gross margin of 84.5% and a net loss of $21.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. Our accumulated deficit as of December 31, 2025 was $146.5 million.

We have invested heavily in product development. Our research and development activities have been centered on driving continuous improvements to our Inspire therapy. We have also made significant investments in clinical studies to demonstrate the safety and efficacy of our Inspire therapy and to support regulatory submissions. We continue to make investments in research and development efforts to develop our future generations of Inspire systems and support our future regulatory submissions for expanded indications and for new markets such as additional European countries and the Asia Pacific region. For example, in August 2024, we received approval from the FDA for our Inspire V neurostimulator ("Inspire V,") which we began to market for sale in the U.S. in May 2025.

Since 2023, glucagon-like peptide 1 ("GLP-1s"), a class of drug indicated for diabetes and obesity, has continued to gain popularity as a weight-loss drug. In late 2024, tirzepatide (marketed as Zepbound), a GLP-1 injection which was FDA approved for weight loss in 2023, was also FDA approved for treatment of OSA in patients with obesity and moderate to severe OSA. If GLP-1s are used to treat OSA in an indication for which Inspire therapy is approved, demand for our Inspire system for patients with that indication could be reduced. OSA is a multifactorial disease with many independent factors including age, gender, weight, and neck circumference. Inspire is designed to address antero-posterior airway collapse, also known as tongue base collapse. In contrast, patients with a higher BMI are subject to a larger neck circumference and present predominantly with lateral-wall collapse.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間醫療科技公司，專注於開發與商業化創新、微創性解決方案，用以治療阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症（"OSA"）患者。本公司自有之 Inspire 系統為首款經美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）、歐盟（"EU"）第 2017/745 號規則（"MDR" 或 "EU 醫療器材規則"）及日本 Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency 認可的神經刺激技術，提供安全有效的治療方案，用以治療中度至重度 OSA 患者。本公司已開發出一種新型閉環解決方案，可持續監測患者的呼吸狀況，並提供輕微的下頜神經刺激，以維持氣道暢通。大量臨牀數據，包括在《新英格蘭醫學期刊》發表的論文、多篇發表於領先的呼吸、耳鼻喉（"ENT"）及睡眠醫學期刊的論文，以及超過 385 篇經同行評審的論文，支持 Inspire 療法的安全性與有效性。Inspire 療法於 2014 年獲 FDA 預市批准（"PMA"），自 2011 年起已在部分歐洲市場商業化。日本厚生勞動省（"MLHW"）於 2018 年批准 Inspire 療法用以治療中度至重度 OSA。Inspire 療法適用於中度至重度 OSA 患者，且患者無顯著的中央型睡眠呼吸中止症，且無軟顎處完全同心性氣道塌陷。醫生已於美國（"U.S."）、歐洲及亞洲治療超過 125,000 名患者使用 Inspire 療法。

睡眠呼吸中止症是一種嚴重且慢性疾病，會對患者的睡眠、健康及生活品質造成負面影響。OSA 是睡眠呼吸中止症最常見的類型。OSA 發生在患者睡眠時，因氣道部分或完全受阻而中斷呼吸，影響所有年齡、性別及體型的患者。OSA 的嚴重程度以患者每小時經歷的 Partial 或 Complete 氣道阻塞次數來衡量，稱為氣道阻塞-低通氣指數（"AHI"）。中度 OSA 患者每小時有 15 到 30 次事件，而重度 OSA 患者每小時有 30 個以上事件。若未治療，OSA 會增加高血壓、高血壓、心力衰竭、中風、冠狀動脈疾病及其他致命疾病的風險。

持續正壓通氣（"CPAP"）是治療中度至重度 OSA 患者的首選療法。CPAP 透過臉部或鼻部面罩連接至牀邊的空氣泵。為使 CPAP 最有效，面罩必須與患者的臉部或鼻部形成氣密封閉，且必須每晚佩戴。CPAP 的有效性受到患者依從性低的限制，因為許多患者認為面罩或治療方式笨重、不舒適且噪音大。當 CPAP 失敗或無法耐受時，患者的其他治療選擇主要為侵入性外科手術，用以修改或移除現有組織以創造自由氣流。這些侵入性外科手術的臨牀效益有限或難以預測，且為不可逆，且可能極為疼痛。

本公司認為，對於 CPAP 的替代方案，仍存在緊迫的臨牀需求與強大的市場機會，此方案應具備有效性與微創性。數據顯示，CPAP 不耐受的 OSA 患者，其死亡風險高於 CPAP 耐受的 OSA 患者，且因心血管健康風險增加而有更高的醫療使用率。2022 年發表於 Medicare 與法國國家醫療保險資料庫的兩項研究結果，顯示在大型國家隊列中，CPAP 不耐受的風險。具體而言，Medicare 中 CPAP 不耐受的患者，其新發心血管事件風險高於依從性患者。同樣地，法國國家補償資料庫顯示，在超過 176,000 名患者中，CPAP 不依從的患者，其死亡風險與新發心力衰竭風險高於依從性患者。這些發現顯示，治療 CPAP 不耐受的 OSA 為改善患者預後及 potentially 減少醫療使用率的迫切需求。
Inspire 療法為一種創新、閉環、微創性解決方案，旨在提供舒適與便利，並使中度至重度 OSA 患者有高依從性。植入後，Inspire 系統會提供電氣刺激，使舌根向前移動，有助維持氣道暢通，使患者能自由無間斷地吸入。本公司認為 Inspire 療法提供以下優點：
•安全、有效且耐用的治療，有強大的臨牀數據支持，包括治療後五年的長期有效性結果。
•閉環系統，使用專利演算法持續監測患者的呼吸，並在吸氣階段提供電氣刺激。
•舒適且便利的治療，導致高患者滿意度，根據本公司持續進行的全球患者登記最新出版物，平均追蹤 12 個月的患者中，有 90% 的患者報告滿意度為 90%。
•強勁的患者依從性，有 80% 的患者在初始治療後五年的 STAR 試驗中持續每晚使用。
•微創的門診手術，恢復時間短。
•長效解決方案，電池設計可持續使用約 11 年，無需充電或維護。
多項臨牀研究的結果，包括七項由本公司贊助及超過 100 項獨立臨牀研究，評估了數千名患者，顯示本公司 Inspire 療法可顯著且持續降低患者 OSA 的嚴重程度，改善與睡眠相關的生活品質，減少打鼾，並具有高患者依從性及強勁的安全性。

我們的關鍵性 STAR 試驗設計用以顯示療法的長期有效性，並包含隨機對照療法中斷研究。長期研究顯示，在中度至重度 OSA 患者中，從基線 29.3 個事件每小時下降至治療後 12 個月的 9.0 個事件每小時，中位數 AHI 降低約 70%。STAR 試驗的追蹤結果在治療後 18 個月、三年及五年時，與初始數據相似。在治療後五年，中度至重度 OSA 患者的中位數 AHI 仍維持在低水平，為 6.2 個事件每小時。隨機對照療法中斷研究的結果進一步顯示 Inspire 療法的有效性，其中療法中斷組的患者 AHI 回升至接近基線水平，而持續療法的控制組患者則持續獲得治療效益。
除了 STAR 試驗，我們已建立全球真實世界患者登記資料庫（"ADHERE"），用以收集植入 Inspire 系統一年後患者的資料，包括安全性、有效性、每週使用情況、整體依從性及滿意度。目標納入 5,000 名患者的目標在 2024 年達成，患者追蹤在 2025 年完成，最終結果尚待分析。如需更多有關 ADHERE 的資訊，請參閱下文「臨牀結果與研究—ADHERE 患者登記資料庫」部分。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的財務報表及其相關附註說明一併閱讀，這些財務報表及附註說明載於本年度10-K表報中其他處。除歷史財務資訊外，以下討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性與假設。部分 herein 所包含的數字為方便呈現而四捨五入。我們實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所預期的有重大差異，原因包括許多因素，包括在本年度10-K表報第一部分「項目1A. 風險因素」及其他處所討論的那些因素。

我們是一家專注於開發與商業化創新、微創解決方案的醫療科技公司，用以治療患有阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症（"OSA"）的病患。我們的專利 Inspire 系統是唯一獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）、歐盟（"EU"）醫療器材法規（"MDR"）及日本 Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency 認證的神經刺激技術，可為患有中度至重度 OSA 的病患提供安全有效的治療。我們已開發出一種新型閉環解決方案，持續監測病患的呼吸情況，並提供輕微的舌下神經刺激以維持氣道開放。Inspire 治療適用於患有中度至重度 OSA 且無顯著中央型睡眠呼吸中止症，且無軟顎水平氣道完全同心塌陷的病患。

我們在美國以及歐洲和日本的部分國家透過直接銷售團隊將 Inspire 系統銷售給醫院與門診手術中心（"ASCs"），而在新加坡、香港及泰國則透過經銷商銷售。我們的直接銷售團隊主要針對耳鼻喉科醫生與睡眠中心進行銷售與促銷活動。此外，我們強調我們強大的臨牀數據與價值主張，以提高轉介醫生對 Inspire 系統的認知與採用率。我們透過強大的直接對消費者行銷活動，進一步推動對 Inspire 系統效益的認知，並透過病患賦權來提高興趣。我們認為這種推廣方式有助於教育數以千計的病患瞭解我們的 Inspire 治療。

雖然我們的銷售與行銷努力針對的是病患與醫生，因為他們是我們技術的主要使用者，但我們認為執行該手術的醫院與 ASCs 是我們的客戶，因為他們是 Inspire 系統的採購者。我們的客戶根據各第三方付款機構（如商業保險機構與政府醫療計畫）的編碼與相關付款方式獲得補償。目前，Inspire 系統對於由商業保險機構投保的病患，按每位病患計為覆蓋；對於由 Medicare 和 Medicare Advantage 投保的病患，按 Local Coverage Determinations 覆蓋；對於由美國政府合同治療的退伍軍人，按美國政府合同覆蓋。截至2026年2月13日，我們已與許多美國商業保險機構取得正面的覆蓋政策，包括所有大型國家商業保險機構，覆蓋美國超過300 百萬名投保人。此外，所有七家 Medicare Administrative Contractors 在符合特定覆蓋標準時，均提供 Inspire 治療的覆蓋。

第三方付款機構要求醫生與醫院使用現行程序術語（"CPT"）編碼，以識別他們尋求補償的服務，這些編碼由美國醫學會（American Medical Association）創建與維護。我們不同世代的 Inspire 治療在歷史上已根據不同的編碼與補償方式進行計費。例如，植入我們的 Inspire IV 裝置的程序在計費時使用的是 Category I CPT 編碼 64582。而在2025年，植入我們的 Inspire V 裝置的程序在計費時使用的是 Category I CPT 編碼 64568。此外，還有其他相關的 CPT 編碼用於修復、移除及 DISE。

2025年11月，2026年 Medicare 補償支付的最終公告已發布。從來到現在，CMS（Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services）與 Medicare Administrative Contractors（"MACs"）以及其他付款機構與補償編碼過程中的相關方，對我們產品的適當補償與編碼仍存在混淆。最近，我們收到了關於 Inspire V 手術應使用編碼的澄清。目前，醫療中心與醫生應根據最新的醫療政策進行計費，無論是 Medicare Administrative Contractor（MACs）或商業保險機構，根據此澄清，我們認為

編碼將轉為 CPT 編碼 64582 用於 Inspire V 手術，包括使用 -52 修改碼。截至目前，我們按體積計算的前三大商業付款機構均已採用 64568 編碼進行 Inspire V 的計費與補償。混淆將持續存在，直到各相關方提供明確且公開的指導，且我們有足夠的申報資料已提交並處理過各付款機構。這些編碼與補償決定可能影響我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果，特別是我們未來的收入。我們持續與相關方合作，以獲得 Inspire V 編碼的具體且準確的指導，包括我們預期會減少 Inspire V 手術在 CPT 編碼 64582 下專業費用約 10% 到 50% 的 -52 修改碼。無論如何，我們認為使用 -52 修改碼導致專業費用顯著減少，可能會影響醫生執行 Inspire V 手術的意願，並可能限制他們選擇執行的病例數量。除了我們短期內的措施，旨在減少實際應用於專業費用的減少，以及推動全國範圍內的一致性外，我們正在尋求長期解決方案，包括建立一個獨立的 CPT 編碼。無法保證 CPT 編碼應用的時間或結果。
其他國家的補償通常可透過私人（商業保險）與公共資金來源，或在醫院層面透過創新預算來建立。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司營業收入中有95.6%來自美國，4.4%來自美國以外地區。沒有任何單一客戶佔本公司營業收入超過10%。
本公司依賴第三方供應商製造Inspire系統及其零組件。許多這些供應商目前為單一來源供應商。目前，本公司所有製造活動均在美國進行，且大多數Inspire系統的零組件均來自美國。本公司過去曾經驗過供應鏈中斷的情況。
本公司通常會維持較高的存貨水準以保護自己免受供應中斷的影響，因此本公司面臨存貨過時及過期的風險，這可能會導致存貨減損費用。例如，在2025年，本公司因與Inspire IV系統相關的過多零組件而記錄了2.1百萬美元的減損費用。

本公司已大量投資於產品開發。本公司研究與開發活動主要聚焦於推動Inspire療法的持續改進。本公司也已投入大量資源於臨牀研究，以證明Inspire療法的安全性與有效性，並支持法規提交。本公司持續投資於研究與開發活動，以開發未來世代的Inspire系統，並支持未來針對擴展適應症與新市場（例如其他歐洲國家及亞太地區）的法規提交。例如，在2024年8月，本公司獲得FDA對Inspire V神經刺激器（"Inspire V"）的批准，本公司於2025年5月開始在美國市場銷售此產品。

自2023年起，GLP-1（"GLP-1s"），一種用於糖尿病與肥胖症的藥物，持續受到歡迎作為減重藥物。在2024年底，tirzepatide（市售名為Zepbound），一種GLP-1注射劑，於2023年獲得FDA批准用於減重，也於2024年獲得FDA批准用於治療肥胖且中度至重度OSA的患者。如果GLP-1s被用於治療OSA的適應症，而Inspire療法已獲得批准，則可能導致本公司Inspire系統在該適應症患者的銷售需求減少。OSA是一種多因素疾病，包含許多獨立因素，包括年齡、性別、體重及頸部週長。Inspire設計用以解決前後氣道塌陷，也稱為舌基塌陷。相對而言，體重較高的患者會有較大的頸部週長，並主要表現為側壁塌陷。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的營業收入主要來自 Inspire 系統的銷售，因此我們的業務成功高度依賴於此係統。
我們的財務表現與普通股的市場價格可能會有顯著波動，且可能無法完全反映我們業務的實際表現。
我們可能無法維持獲利，我們歷來已產生重大營運虧損，未來也可能產生營運虧損。
我們的長期成長取決於我們能否提升 Inspire 系統、擴大適應症範圍，並開發與商業化其他產品。
若我們無法準確預測客戶對 Inspire 系統的需求並管理存貨，我們的營運結果可能會受到重大影響。
我們的運輸業者若發生運輸問題、服務中斷或價格上漲，可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響，並損害我們的聲譽與及時提供服務的能力。
若我們無法有效評估、管理與維護我們的直接銷售與行銷組織，我們可能無法實現營收成長。
為成功行銷與銷售我們的 Inspire 系統於美國以外之市場，我們必須應對許多國際商業風險。
我們面臨產品責任索償之風險，此風險可能造成高昂費用、分散管理階層之注意力，並損害本公司之聲譽與業務。我們可能無法維持足夠之產品責任保險。
若我們的 Inspire 系統品質未符合醫師或病患之期待，則本公司之品牌與聲譽或業務可能受到不利影響。
若我們選擇取得新且具補充性之業務、產品或技術，我們可能無法完成這些併購，或以成本效益且不幹擾之方式成功整合之。
不利之全球經濟條件可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成不利影響。
關鍵資訊科技系統、流程或場地之失敗、網路攻擊，或其他資訊安全之缺失，可能對本公司之業務與營運造成不利影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。這些風險包括但不限於下列所描述的風險，每項風險都可能影響投資決策。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並與本年度10-K表報表所包含或參考的其他資訊一併考量。任何上述風險的實現都可能對本公司聲譽、業務、財務狀況、營運結果、成長以及達成戰略目標的能力產生重大負面影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能會下跌。其他我們目前未預期或認為不重要的事件，也可能影響本公司聲譽、業務、財務狀況、營運結果、成長以及達成戰略目標的能力。

我們自2011年起在某些歐洲國家開始銷售Inspire系統，2014年起在美國銷售，2021年起在某些亞太地區銷售。我們Inspire系統的銷售，主要佔我們2025年、2024年及2023年財年營收的全部。我們預期未來Inspire系統的銷售仍將佔我們營收的絕大多數。因此，我們執行成長策略並維持獲利的能力，將取決於患者、醫生及睡眠中心等各方，對我們Inspire療法用來治療中度至重度OSA患者的接受度，特別是那些無法使用或無法持續受益於CPAP的患者。
我們無法確保Inspire療法會獲得或維持醫生與患者廣泛的市場接受度。作為一家單一產品公司，若Inspire系統無法滿足醫生或患者的需求數或無法獲得有意義的市場接受度，將會對我們的業務與未來前景造成傷害。

本公司普通股的市場價格以及我們每季與每年的營運結果，在過去與未來都可能有顯著波動，因此未來各期間的營運結果比較可能不具意義。因此，任何一個季度或期間的結果不應被視為未來表現的指標。本公司普通股的市場價格以及我們每季與每年的財務結果可能因多種因素而波動，許多因素在本公司控制範圍之外，因此可能無法完全反映本公司業務的實際表現。這些因素可能包括，例如，銷售的季節性變動或在健康危機期間進行的選擇性手術程序延後，如COVID-19的情況。
我們通常在美國第四季會有較高的銷售，這是因為患者已支付年度保險免賠額，從而減少其自付費用。反之，在第一季，許多美國患者的保險免賠額重置，導致更高的自付費用，這會在該期間對我們的銷售造成負面影響。
其他可能導致本公司普通股市場價格高度波動以及我們每季與每年結果出現波動的因素包括，但不限於：
